key_insight: The paper turns 2D Stokes flow in irregular domains into a boundary-only algebraic problem on an unfitted MAC grid, using lattice Green’s functions and Calderón preconditioning to achieve accurate, stable solves without fitted meshes or singular quadrature.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical high-accuracy solver for complex-fluid geometries such as obstacles, narrow gaps, and multiply connected domains, with strong conditioning and near mesh-independent performance for exterior problems.
method: Builds velocity/pressure homogeneous solutions from free-space lattice Green’s functions on thin staggered boundary layers
Imposes Dirichlet data at cut points by local interpolation and removes hydrostatic null modes with sampled-normal rank updates
Solves the dense boundary system with GMRES plus a componentwise discrete Calderón preconditioner accelerated by padded FFTs
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive validation on multiple challenging geometries, showing second-order convergence in velocity and pressure, discrete divergence at solver accuracy, recovery of Moffatt eddy scaling, and orders-of-magnitude condition-number reduction.
watch_item: The preconditioner remains effective but more demanding in narrow-gap and fine-grid interior cases, so memory/compute cost and robustness near tight clearances may be a practical concern.
paper_title: An unfitted boundary algebraic equation method with Calderón preconditioning for 2D Stokes flow in irregular geometry
